word_order: SOV | Verbs and verbal predicates consistently appear at the end of clauses/sentences (e.g., 働き始め、その主任彫版工となりました; 回収したと報じました).
register: written news/encyclopedic prose (formal, edited informative text such as news reports or encyclopedia/Wikipedia-style articles)
clause_boundary_signals: ます／ました／です／だ (sentence-final polite/plain predicates)
〜となりました／〜なりました (resultative copula endings)
と報じました／と述べました／と主張して (quotative + reporting verb)
〜し (end of clause in a list when it is the last predicate it also closes)
〜て (連用形/て形 when followed by sentence-final predicate it may join; when used sentence-final it marks continuation only rarely)
non_boundary_traps: という (noun-modifier or name-quotative inside NPs)
て (conjunctive て-form: looks like an ending but usually connects to following clause)
し (listing/contrastive connective that may not end the overall predicate)
た (past-tense verb form when it is a modifier before a noun: relative clause)
unstable_prefix_signals: て (verb て-form — signals continuation; do not split immediately after it)
し (conjunctive し — often continues or completes a list of predicates)
と (quotative/conditional: the clause may continue with a reporting verb or conditional result)
という (can be a clause-final quote marker or a noun-modifying phrase; subsequent words can change its role)
の／こと (nominalizers that often lead into further explanation)
notes_for_prompt_writer: Prefer emitting segments at sentence-final predicates (polite/plain endings like ます/た/だ/です) and before major discourse-openers such as また／一方. Avoid splitting immediately after connective suffixes and particles (て／し／と／の／という／ため) because they commonly continue the clause or convert it into a modifier. Treat quoted titles or quoted clauses as single units until a clear reporting verb or sentence-final predicate follows.
